title: Pre-register a GQ-010 baseline BEFORE merges change the graph
evidence: GQ-010's own evidence_gaps[0]: no agreed baseline exists for evidence-retrieval time or decision changes.

spec.description: GQ-010 has no baseline, so nothing downstream of it is measurable. This is TIME-CRITICAL in a way the other tasks are not: once the merges land, today's graph is gone and the before-picture cannot be reconstructed.
spec.context: Pre-register 5 real decisions and time them against TODAY's graph before any merge changes it. Pre-registration must be frozen before the first measurement, and the module's own experimental-method.md makes the point that a Git commit should not replace an external preregistration - timestamp it somewhere not controlled by the analyst. Without this, any later claim that the work improved retrieval or decision quality is unfalsifiable. BASELINE NOW EXISTS: PG-BASELINE captured it 2026-08-07 against the shipped asset before any consolidation PR was merged -- see consolidation-source/GQ-010-BASELINE.html. It records the five pre-registered decisions (written before any query ran), the 0-of-6 criterion score, and F3/F5 already firing. REMAINING WORK: the baseline explicitly states it could NOT measure human evidence-retrieval time, only sub-second machine latency, and warns that any future '80% faster' claim must time the analyst loop rather than sqlite3 wall-clock. That measurement is still owed.
acceptance_criteria: 5 decisions pre-registered with their measurement protocol frozen before the first timing
Timings recorded against the pre-merge graph
The registration is timestamped outside the analyst's own control
